description:
Problem: the sweep job in .github/workflows/oracle-gate.yml runs _project/scripts/oracle_gate.py for every open develop pull request and records the pull request as failed when the script exits non-zero. The script returns PASS (0), WAITING (1) or ERROR (2). WAITING means the gate correctly posted failure because the pull request is not ready yet, for example while it waits for an oracle review. That is a successful evaluation, but the sweep counts it as a failure and exits non-zero. Every schedule sweep since at least 2026-10-24 (runs 40101016116, 40116686358, 40126613035, 40139722596, 40151094620) and the first push sweep (40165045688) concluded failure, listing only waiting pull requests. A real evaluation error is therefore indistinguishable from normal waiting, and the run is always red. Python also exits 1 for an uncaught exception, so exempting exit 1 would hide crashes (oracle defect D1 on PR #3438).

Outcome: oracle_gate.py's process exit code for WAITING is a dedicated value, 3, that neither Python nor uv uses for failures. main()'s return values (PASS 0, WAITING 1, ERROR 2) and every caller of main() are unchanged. The sweep treats exits 0 and 3 as evaluated and records any other code as failed, with the code in its warning.

Decision gates (stop and report if one fails):
1. Confirm the exit-code contract in oracle_gate.py: PASS 0, WAITING 1, ERROR 2. Confirm that main() posts a status before returning WAITING, so a waiting pull request already carries its failure status.
2. Confirm nothing else, such as alerting, another workflow or a doc, relies on the sweep run failing when pull requests are waiting, or on oracle_gate.py exiting 1 for WAITING.

Item guardrails: main()'s return values, decide(), the App binding and posting are unchanged. Only the script's process exit mapping (WAITING to 3, at the __main__ boundary) and the sweep's classification change. This narrows the original guardrail, which forbade any exit-code change, because the oracle showed that exit 1 cannot safely mean WAITING. The gate job keeps failing on any non-zero exit.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Close out with make pr-preflight, make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, then make pr-arm. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). Every behavior change gets a test that fails on the previous code.
